unmapped_findings: Actual measured chemical composition of the 0.04Nb steel strip (wt%): Mn 12.82, Al 9.12, Cr 2.99, C 1.40, Nb 0.039, Fe balance (Table 1).
Quantitative chemical composition of austenite in the as-cast 0.04Nb steel (wt%): Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038, Fe 64.07 (Table 4).
The austenite grain size of as-cast 0.04Nb steel (9 μm) is approximately half that of as-cast 0.02Nb steel (18 μm), attributed to NbC precipitation.
The yield strength of 0.04Nb steels exceeds that of 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa, mainly due to additional fine grain strengthening and dislocation strengthening.
Nb doping significantly increases the formation energy of κ-carbide (0.891 eV for Fe24Al8C8 vs 2.826 eV for Fe23NbAl8C8 and 1.453 eV for Fe24Al7NbC8).
NbC precipitation temperature increases from ≈973 K to 1573 K as Nb content increases from 0 to 0.05 wt% (Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase diagram).
